claims.text: the 10-trit payload is chosen by the request: with ONE fixed 293-byte image, four different requests produce four different exact payloads (93, 187, 281, 29797), each written exactly in the epoch cell and executed there (OUT = V % 256 at pc = T = 100)
the request is consumed in order: the 20 control bytes are read in sequence and each one lands in its own position
the payload is not fixed in the program: mutating a single request byte changes the written payload (29797 -> 29798)
the decomposition V = crazy(M, P) with P = 29524 + sum(3^p for trit_p(V)=1) and M = 29524 + sum(3^p for trit_p(V)!=0), both in {1,2}^10, holds for ALL 59049 words (exhaustive, 0 mismatches)

NEGATIVE: the trit -> control-digit map that would let the request carry the 10 trits directly ((0,2,0) or (0,2,2)) is NOT reachable by any composition of crazy: the semigroup over one trit has exactly 15 maps and neither is among them ((0,0,2) is reachable). The interface therefore carries control digits
two independent Python engines agree byte for byte with the repo oracle (traced repo oracle + traced native_classic)

the C runner executes the whole program when the payload is printable (V = 93: same OUT 0x5d, 171 steps) and stops at the printable guard otherwise (step 170, exactly the step predicted from the oracle trace, see c_printable_guard_v1)

the epoch cell is still chosen by the program (T = 100 fixed); combining the request-driven epoch selection of epoch_algebra_v3 with this request-driven payload, and rearming the epoch for a second request in the same run, is NOT yet done
